findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()
findings.body: The code calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` without arguments, but the only such method defined in the parent class `UsernamePasswordForm` is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` which requires a `UserModel` parameter. No no-arg overload exists in `UsernameForm`, `UsernamePasswordForm`, or `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` (all shown in full). This will fail to compile. The call likely needs to be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` or a separate no-arg convenience method needs to be added.

findings.title: WebAuthn conditional UI no longer set up during initial login (user is null)
findings.body: The `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` check requires `user != null`, but during initial login `context.getUser()` is null. The previous code (`webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`) was inside the `else` branch (user == null) and correctly set up the WebAuthn challenge for initial login. With this change, `fillContextForm` is never called during initial login, so no WebAuthn challenge is generated and the browser cannot perform the passkey ceremony. This breaks the discoverable-key auto-login flow (e.g., `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey` expects automatic login on initial page load). The condition should likely be `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` (without the user != null requirement) or should handle both cases separately.

findings.title: Inverted condition in challenge() breaks WebAuthn on initial-login error pages
findings.body: The overridden `challenge(context, error, field)` now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` which requires user != null. The previous code was `context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` — it set up WebAuthn when user was null (initial login errors). During initial login with a wrong password, `context.getUser()` is null at the time `challenge()` is called (the user is only set in context after successful password validation), so WebAuthn will no longer appear on the error page. This means a user who mistypes their password on the combined username/password form can no longer recover by using a passkey.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled conflates 'passkeys enabled' with 'user is set'
findings.body: The method `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. This conflates two independent concerns: whether the passkeys feature is enabled, and whether a user is present in the context. Callers in `authenticate()` and `challenge()` need different semantics (initial login has no user but still needs WebAuthn; re-authentication has a user and also needs WebAuthn). A clearer design would separate the feature-enabled check from the user-presence check, or provide distinct methods for each scenario.
